Title: Cross-domain generalisation of physiological stress detection
How close it is to our method: Very close, uses baseline normalization for WESAD to SWELL-KW transfer.
How our paper differs: Our paper explicitly diagnoses the modality-specific shift (ACC vs Physio) and uses SHAP to prove attribution agreement.

Title: Subject-independent stress detection using wearable sensors
How close it is to our method: Internal WESAD only, but emphasizes baseline normalization.
How our paper differs: We evaluate strict zero-shot external transfer rather than just internal LOSO.

Title: A Deep Learning Approach to Cross-Dataset Stress Detection
How close it is to our method: Uses WESAD and external data, but relies on domain adaptation (target labels).
How our paper differs: We focus on zero-shot transfer without any target-side adaptation, proving absolute baseline normalization is sufficient.

Title: Feature Importance in Physiological Stress Detection
How our paper differs: We compute cross-dataset SHAP agreement to prove the learned representation is robust.

Title: Generalizability of Heart Rate Variability in Stress Detection
How close it is to our method: Focuses on HRV (BVP). Uses baseline norm.
How our paper differs: We provide a multimodal factorial ablation (ACC + EDA/BVP/TEMP) and demonstrate 1.000 recovery.
